fixes.explanation: That's right, baker. Peter says, “But God raised Him from the dead, releasing Him from the agony of death, because it was impossible for death to keep Him in its grip.” So the statement is true. Impossible. Death had its grip out and couldn't hold on.
You caught it, baker. Peter's reason is the time of day: “It is only the third hour of the day!” Nothing in his words says it's late at night. The third hour is Peter's whole case.

I see why you'd think it. But in the words Peter quotes from Joel, God says He will pour out His Spirit “…on all people.” Then He names sons and daughters, young men, old men, and menservants and maidservants. Priests aren't named at all.

Yes, baker, yes, that's true. Joel's words, as Peter quotes them, end with this: “And everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.” Wonders in the sky come first, but the promise is what lands last. Everyone who calls, saved.
I get it, Hades sounds scary. But David says, “…I will not be shaken. Therefore my heart is glad and my tongue rejoices…” Afraid isn't the word he uses for his heart. Glad is.

Hades isn't a cheerful word, so troubled makes sense. But David says, “Therefore my heart is glad and my tongue rejoices; my body also will dwell in hope…” That comes right after he says God will not abandon his soul to Hades. Troubled isn't the word he uses. Glad is.
That's right, baker. Peter says, “God has raised this Jesus to life, to which we are all witnesses.” It's “we,” not just “I.” Peter stood up with the Eleven, and he says “all.”

That's the one. The people were cut to the heart, and they asked Peter and the other apostles, “Brothers, what shall we do?” Their question is about what to do next. Peter replies in the very next verse.
That question sounds natural for a crowd that's been cut to the heart. But the text doesn't have them say it. They ask, “Brothers, what shall we do?” That's a question about what to do next.

Yes, baker, yes! Peter says, “Repent and be baptized, every one of you, in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins…” Notice “…every one of you…” Nobody gets a pass, and nobody gets left out.

Praying is good, and the believers do it later in this very passage. But it's not what Peter tells this crowd to do. He says, “Repent and be baptized, every one of you, in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins…” Those are the two things: repent and be baptized.

Doubts, friend? I had plenty back in that junk drawer I lived in for years. But Peter doesn't say doubts. He says to be baptized “…in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins…” Sins is the word, and it's a big one.
That's right, baker. The text says, “…about three thousand were added to the believers that day.” That is a LOT of people added in a single day. I'd lose count somewhere around forty.

Anger, huh? I get that way over a jammed oven door, so I understand the guess. But the text says, “A sense of awe came over everyone, and the apostles performed many wonders and signs.” The word is awe, and it came over everyone.
